items.title: Joseph Daley interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 18, 2018
items.q: we love Duke Ellington and Thelonious Monk and all those great musicians just as much as the people that play the tradition also.

ctx.x: Well it’s not that much different than the transition from swing music into bop then. Those guys were expanding the tradition.

Right. That’s exactly what has happened. And you know, bop was, people said bop wasn’t, I mean here, the description they gave for bop, bop wasn’t for dancing, well that’s not true. I mean if you see the people doing the lindy hop and all that stuff, you know, at those very fast tempos, you know, so people danced to bop just like they did to swing. It’s just that swing was, the tempos of swing were not as fast as the tempos for bop. So you had to have some serious dancing skill to dance to bebop, whereas dancing…
I was talking with Warren yesterday a bit about Max Roach.
